name: Dimorphodon
sum: Big-headed Early Jurassic pterosaur from the Blue Lias of England, named for its two kinds of teeth.
wsnote: About 1.45 m; body length about 1 m.
holotype: NHMUK PV R1034 — Blue Lias, Lyme Regis, Dorset (found 1828, Mary Anning).
material: Partial disarticulated skeleton without skull; skulls known from NHMUK PV OR 41212 and R1035.
biology: Deep, lightly built skull with fangs at the front and tiny lancet teeth behind. Dental microwear supports a predator of small vertebrates that may also have taken insects.
